review.algorithm_assessment: For a bridge, deleting it separates components of sizes s and n-s; any reconnection between them preserves a cactus, except the identical old edge. For a cycle edge, deletion merges that cycle vertices bridge-only components into one tree. A legal new cycle must use only bridges, so count nonedges within every bridge-only tree component after the deletion, excluding the old edge. DSU gives original bridge-component sizes; each cycle contributes its length times the same merged-component pair count. Iterative DFS identifies all cactus cycles and bridge subtree sizes in linear time.
